data.body:
PUSHED for review: Gerrit change 1146, commit ead36bdb2, on top of a49e (1140).
Trailers verified: rebar-ticket resolves to this ticket, Change-Id stamped, DCO signed.
Pre-commit gates all passed; make lint and make typecheck clean on the final tree (405 files).

A TEST-ISOLATION GAP THIS CHANGE INTRODUCED, found and fixed in the same commit. Wiring class
resolution into sizing.models_at_or_above and config.resolve_model makes those two functions read
CONFIGURATION where they previously read only the MODEL_LADDER constant. That created a new
ambient-environment dependency for every test that asserts a literal bare model id.

Diagnosed by experiment rather than by reasoning, because the two config layers behave
differently:
  LAYER 1, project config: NOT exposed. Added a [tool.rebar.llm.model_classes] Bedrock table to
    rebar's own pyproject.toml and ran the exposed tests: 8 passed. The suite's autouse fixture
    pins REBAR_ROOT to a scratch repo, so the real pyproject is never read. Already isolated.
  LAYER 2, the nine REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_<FIELD> env vars: EXPOSED, nothing scrubbed them. With
    REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL + _PROVIDER exported (exactly what an operator retargeting the
    standard class onto Bedrock has set), test_plan_review.py::test_is_context_limit_error_and_
    ladder FAILS at :1145, index 1 becoming bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6. That failure
    names an unrelated test and reads as a size-ladder regression, so it is expensive to diagnose.

FIX: an autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py delenv's all nine, matching the file's existing
env-hygiene idiom (_identity_enforcement_off_by_default). UNCONDITIONAL, like the identity guard
rather than the compaction-horizon default, because the point is to override a stray ambient value
rather than defer to it. Verified BOTH directions: the ambient-override experiment now passes
(7 passed), and the tests that exercise the override MECHANISM still pass (54 passed in
test_model_classes.py + test_model_class_ladder.py + test_llm_fallback_chain.py) because their own
monkeypatch.setenv runs after every fixture and still wins.

This gap would have fired the moment this project configures classes for the S8 Bedrock cutover,
i.e. inside this same epic.

STILL OUTSTANDING before this ticket can close: Verified +1 on 1146, and the full local suite
(running; the six directly-implicated suites are 168 passed and tests/unit/workflow is 498 passed).

UNRELATED BOARD OBSERVATION for whoever picks this up: change 1132 (8229, an ANCESTOR of this
change) currently has NO LLM-Review vote. History shows the review bot voted LLM-Review -1 with
"coverage-gap (review-error)" -- the code review could not run, fail-closed -- then the operator
voted +1 and then REMOVED both that -1 and their own +1. Since submit requirements are inherited
down the stack, 1132 needs a clean bot review before anything above it can submit. Left alone
deliberately: this is an operator action in flight, not a defect to work around.
